review.title: Improper election practices and disqualification of electors
review.plain: The Legislature shall prohibit improper practices that affect elections and shall provide for disqualifying electors while mentally incompetent or serving a state or federal prison term for a felony conviction.

provisions.what: The Legislature shall prohibit improper practices that affect elections
requires: prohibit improper practices that affect elections

provisions.what: The Legislature shall provide for the disqualification of electors while mentally incompetent or serving a state or federal prison term for the conviction of a felony
requires: provide for the disqualification of electors while mentally incompetent or serving a state or federal prison term for the conviction of a felony

review.title: Voter-nominated (top-two) primary elections
review.plain: A voter-nominated primary selects candidates for congressional and state offices; all voters may vote for any candidate regardless of party preference, and the top two compete in the general election. Parties may not nominate at that primary. The Legislature shall provide for partisan presidential and party elections.
rights: may vote at a voter-nominated primary election for any candidate
may have his or her political party preference, or lack of political party preference, indicated upon the ballot
has the right to participate in the general election for that office
limits: shall not nominate a candidate for any congressional or state elective office at the voter-nominated primary
shall not have the right to have its preferred candidate participate in the general election
shall not be denied the ability to place on the general election ballot the candidate

provisions.what: A voter-nomination primary election shall be conducted to select the candidates for congressional and state elective offices in California

All voters may vote at a voter-nominated primary election for any candidate for congressional and state elective office without regard to the political party preference disclosed by the candidate or the voter
conditions: provided that the voter is otherwise qualified to vote for candidates for the office in question

provisions.what: The candidates who are the top two vote-getters at a voter-nominated primary election for a congressional or state elective office shall, regardless of party preference, compete in the ensuing general election

A candidate for a congressional or state elective office may have his or her political party preference, or lack of political party preference, indicated upon the ballot for the office in the manner provided by statute
provisions.holder: A candidate for a congressional or state elective office
exceptions: Except as otherwise provided by Section 6

provisions.what: A political party or party central committee shall not nominate a candidate for any congressional or state elective office at the voter-nominated primary
provisions.binds: A political party or party central committee
forbids: nominate a candidate for any congressional or state elective office at the voter-nominated primary
exceptions: This subdivision shall not be interpreted to prohibit a political party or party central committee from endorsing, supporting, or opposing any candidate for a congressional or state elective office

provisions.what: A political party or party central committee shall not have the right to have its preferred candidate participate in the general election for a voter-nominated office other than a candidate who is one of the two highest vote-getters at the primary election
provisions.binds: A political party or party central committee
exceptions: a candidate who is one of the two highest vote-getters at the primary election, as provided in subdivision (a)

provisions.what: The Legislature shall provide for partisan elections for presidential candidates, and political party and party central committees, including an open presidential primary
requires: provide for partisan elections for presidential candidates, and political party and party central committees

including an open presidential primary whereby the candidates on the ballot are those found by the Secretary of State to be recognized candidates throughout the nation or throughout California for the office of President of the United States, and those whose names are placed on the ballot by petition
exceptions: excluding any candidate who has withdrawn by filing an affidavit of noncandidacy

provisions.what: A political party that participated in a primary election for a partisan office pursuant to subdivision (c) has the right to participate in the general election for that office and shall not be denied the ability to place on the general election ballot the candidate who received, at the primary election, the highest vote among that party’s candidates
provisions.holder: A political party that participated in a primary election for a partisan office pursuant to subdivision (c)
conditions: participated in a primary election for a partisan office pursuant to subdivision (c)

review.title: Nonpartisan offices
review.plain: All judicial, school, county, and city offices, including the Superintendent of Public Instruction, shall be nonpartisan. Parties shall not nominate candidates for nonpartisan office, and a candidate's party preference shall not be on the ballot.
limits: shall not nominate a candidate for nonpartisan office
shall not be included on the ballot for the nonpartisan office

provisions.what: All judicial, school, county, and city offices, including the Superintendent of Public Instruction, shall be nonpartisan
A political party or party central committee shall not nominate a candidate for nonpartisan office
provisions.binds: A political party or party central committee
forbids: nominate a candidate for nonpartisan office

provisions.what: The candidate’s party preference shall not be included on the ballot for the nonpartisan office
forbids: including the candidate’s party preference on the ballot for the nonpartisan office

review.title: Secret ballot
review.plain: Voting shall be secret.

provisions.what: Voting shall be secret
requires: Voting shall be secret

review.title: The initiative
review.plain: The initiative is the electors' power to propose and adopt or reject statutes and constitutional amendments, by petition signed by a set share of voters. The Secretary of State submits a qualified measure at an election. Measures may embrace only one subject and are limited in other ways.
powers: The initiative is the power of the electors to propose statutes and amendments to the Constitution and to adopt or reject them
may call a special statewide election for the measure
limits: may not be submitted to the electors or have any effect
may not include or exclude any political subdivision of the State from the application or effect of its provisions
may not contain alternative or cumulative provisions

provisions.what: The initiative is the power of the electors to propose statutes and amendments to the Constitution and to adopt or reject them
terms: "The initiative": the power of the electors to propose statutes and amendments to the Constitution and to adopt or reject them

provisions.what: An initiative measure may be proposed by presenting to the Secretary of State a petition that sets forth the text of the proposed statute or amendment to the Constitution and is certified to have been signed by electors equal in number to 5 percent in the case of a statute, and 8 percent in the case of an amendment to the Constitution, of the votes for all candidates for Governor at the last gubernatorial election
requires: a petition that sets forth the text of the proposed statute or amendment to the Constitution

certified to have been signed by electors equal in number to 5 percent in the case of a statute, and 8 percent in the case of an amendment to the Constitution, of the votes for all candidates for Governor at the last gubernatorial election

provisions.what: The Secretary of State shall then submit the measure at the next general election held at least 131 days after it qualifies or at any special statewide election held prior to that general election
requires: submit the measure at the next general election held at least 131 days after it qualifies or at any special statewide election held prior to that general election

provisions.what: The Governor may call a special statewide election for the measure
An initiative measure embracing more than one subject may not be submitted to the electors or have any effect
forbids: submitting to the electors an initiative measure embracing more than one subject

provisions.what: An initiative measure may not include or exclude any political subdivision of the State from the application or effect of its provisions based upon approval or disapproval of the initiative measure, or based upon the casting of a specified percentage of votes in favor of the measure, by the electors of that political subdivision
forbids: include or exclude any political subdivision of the State from the application or effect of its provisions based upon approval or disapproval of the initiative measure, or based upon the casting of a specified percentage of votes in favor of the measure, by the electors of that political subdivision

provisions.what: An initiative measure may not contain alternative or cumulative provisions wherein one or more of those provisions would become law depending upon the casting of a specified percentage of votes for or against the measure
forbids: contain alternative or cumulative provisions wherein one or more of those provisions would become law depending upon the casting of a specified percentage of votes for or against the measure

review.title: The referendum
review.plain: The referendum is the electors' power to approve or reject statutes, except urgency statutes, statutes calling elections, and tax levy or usual current expense appropriation statutes. A petition signed by 5 percent of the last gubernatorial vote, filed within 90 days, puts the statute to the voters.
powers: The referendum is the power of the electors to approve or reject statutes or parts of statutes
may call a special statewide election for the measure
limits: the petition may not be presented on or after January 1 next following the enactment date

provisions.what: The referendum is the power of the electors to approve or reject statutes or parts of statutes
exceptions: except urgency statutes, statutes calling elections, and statutes providing for tax levies or appropriations for usual current expenses of the State
terms: "The referendum": the power of the electors to approve or reject statutes or parts of statutes except urgency statutes, statutes calling elections, and statutes providing for tax levies or appropriations for usual current expenses of the State

provisions.what: A referendum measure may be proposed by presenting to the Secretary of State, within 90 days after the enactment date of the statute, a petition certified to have been signed by electors equal in number to 5 percent of the votes for all candidates for Governor at the last gubernatorial election, asking that the statute or part of it be submitted to the electors
requires: within 90 days after the enactment date of the statute
a petition certified to have been signed by electors equal in number to 5 percent of the votes for all candidates for Governor at the last gubernatorial election

requires: submit the measure at the next general election held at least 31 days after it qualifies or at a special statewide election held prior to that general election

review.title: When measures take effect; amendment; petitions
review.plain: An approved initiative statute or referendum takes effect on the fifth day after the statement of the vote is filed. When approved measures conflict, the one with the most affirmative votes prevails. The Legislature may amend or repeal initiative statutes only with voter approval unless the initiative permits otherwise.
powers: The Legislature may amend or repeal a referendum statute
The Legislature may amend or repeal an initiative statute
limits: shall not be delayed from going into effect

provisions.what: An initiative statute or referendum approved by a majority of votes cast thereon takes effect on the fifth day after the Secretary of State files the statement of the vote for the election at which the measure is voted on
conditions: approved by a majority of votes cast thereon
exceptions: the measure may provide that it becomes operative after its effective date

provisions.what: If a referendum petition is filed against a part of a statute, the remainder of the statute shall not be delayed from going into effect
forbids: delaying the remainder of the statute from going into effect
conditions: If a referendum petition is filed against a part of a statute

provisions.what: If provisions of two or more measures approved at the same election conflict, the provisions of the measure receiving the highest number of affirmative votes shall prevail
conditions: If provisions of two or more measures approved at the same election conflict

provisions.what: The Legislature may amend or repeal a referendum statute
The Legislature may amend or repeal an initiative statute by another statute that becomes effective only when approved by the electors
requires: by another statute that becomes effective only when approved by the electors
exceptions: unless the initiative statute permits amendment or repeal without the electors’ approval

prepare a title and summary of the measure as provided by law
conditions: Before circulation of an initiative or referendum petition for signatures

provisions.what: The Legislature shall provide for the manner in which a petition shall be circulated, presented, and certified, and the manner in which a measure shall be submitted to the electors
requires: provide for the manner in which a petition shall be circulated, presented, and certified
provide for the manner in which a measure shall be submitted to the electors

review.title: Local initiative and referendum
review.plain: Electors of each city or county may exercise initiative and referendum powers under procedures the Legislature shall provide. City or county initiatives may not include or exclude parts of the area based on how they vote, or contain alternative or cumulative provisions depending on vote percentages.
powers: Initiative and referendum powers may be exercised by the electors of each city or county
limits: may not include or exclude any part of the city or county from the application or effect of its provisions
may not contain alternative or cumulative provisions

provisions.what: Initiative and referendum powers may be exercised by the electors of each city or county under procedures that the Legislature shall provide
provisions.holder: The electors of each city or county
requires: procedures that the Legislature shall provide
exceptions: Except as provided in subdivisions (b) and (c), this section does not affect a city having a charter

provisions.what: A city or county initiative measure may not include or exclude any part of the city or county from the application or effect of its provisions based upon approval or disapproval of the initiative measure, or based upon the casting of a specified percentage of votes in favor of the measure, by the electors of the city or county or any part thereof
forbids: include or exclude any part of the city or county from the application or effect of its provisions based upon approval or disapproval of the initiative measure, or based upon the casting of a specified percentage of votes in favor of the measure

review.title: Measures naming individuals or corporations
review.plain: No constitutional amendment, and no statute proposed to the electors by the Legislature or by initiative, that names an individual to hold office or names a private corporation to perform a function or have a power or duty may be submitted to the electors or have any effect.
limits: No amendment to the Constitution, and no statute proposed to the electors

provisions.what: No amendment to the Constitution, and no statute proposed to the electors by the Legislature or by initiative, that names any individual to hold any office, or names or identifies any private corporation to perform any function or to have any power or duty, may be submitted to the electors or have any effect
forbids: submitting to the electors an amendment or statute that names any individual to hold any office
submitting to the electors an amendment or statute that names or identifies any private corporation to perform any function or to have any power or duty

review.title: The recall
review.plain: Recall is the power of the electors to remove an elective officer.
powers: Recall is the power of the electors to remove an elective officer

provisions.what: Recall is the power of the electors to remove an elective officer
terms: "Recall": the power of the electors to remove an elective officer

review.title: Recall petitions for state officers
review.plain: Recall of a state officer starts with a petition to the Secretary of State alleging a reason, which is not reviewable; proponents have 160 days to file. It sets signature thresholds for statewide and other officers, and the Secretary of State keeps a continuous count.
limits: Sufficiency of reason is not reviewable

provisions.what: Recall of a state officer is initiated by delivering to the Secretary of State a petition alleging reason for recall
requires: a petition alleging reason for recall

provisions.what: Sufficiency of reason is not reviewable
Proponents have 160 days to file signed petitions

A petition to recall a statewide officer must be signed by electors equal in number to 12 percent of the last vote for the office, with signatures from each of 5 counties equal in number to 1 percent of the last vote for the office in the county
requires: signed by electors equal in number to 12 percent of the last vote for the office
signatures from each of 5 counties equal in number to 1 percent of the last vote for the office in the county

provisions.what: Signatures to recall Senators, members of the Assembly, members of the Board of Equalization, and judges of courts of appeal and trial courts must equal in number 20 percent of the last vote for the office
requires: equal in number 20 percent of the last vote for the office

review.title: Recall elections
review.plain: The Governor shall call a recall election within 60 to 80 days of certification, or within 180 days to consolidate with a regular election. If a majority votes to recall, the officer is removed and the plurality candidate succeeds; the officer may not be a candidate.
powers: A recall election may be conducted within 180 days
limits: The officer may not be a candidate

provisions.what: An election to determine whether to recall an officer and, if appropriate, to elect a successor shall be called by the Governor and held not less than 60 days nor more than 80 days from the date of certification of sufficient signatures
requires: called by the Governor
held not less than 60 days nor more than 80 days from the date of certification of sufficient signatures

provisions.what: A recall election may be conducted within 180 days from the date of certification of sufficient signatures in order that the election may be consolidated with the next regularly scheduled election occurring wholly or partially within the same jurisdiction
conditions: if the number of voters eligible to vote at that next regularly scheduled election equal at least 50 percent of all the voters eligible to vote at the recall election

provisions.what: If the majority vote on the question is to recall, the officer is removed and, if there is a candidate, the candidate who receives a plurality is the successor

review.title: Start of terms of elective offices
review.plain: Terms of elective offices provided for by this Constitution, other than Members of the Legislature, commence on the Monday after January 1 following election. The election is held in the last even-numbered year before the term expires.

review.title: California part of the United States
review.plain: The State of California is an inseparable part of the United States of America, and the United States Constitution is the supreme law of the land.

review.title: Separation of powers
review.plain: The powers of state government are legislative, executive, and judicial. Persons charged with exercising one power may not exercise either of the others except as this Constitution permits.
